title: Mechanisms of Cell Death in Spinal Muscular Atrophy
brief_summary: Spinal muscular atrophy is a genetically based disease that affects motor neurons in the spinal cord and leads to muscle wasting and weakness. The gene found to be responsible for the underlying disease is called the SMN or survival motor neuron gene. Individuals with SMA are either missing a copy of the gene or have a mutation in the gene. Although the gene has been identified, how it actually causes the motor neurons to die and leads to muscle wasting and weakness is not completely understood. The investigators have found that skin cells from children with SMA tend to be more susceptible to cell death when exposed to cell death inducing agents. In this protocol, The investigators wish to study the mechanisms by which these cells die when exposed to these agents and how this may be related to the gene defect and the disease.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of SMA confirmed by neurologist

Exclusion Criteria:

* Not seen as a patient at a participating Nemours facility
study_population: This study will enroll Children with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA)
